hypothesis: Staging each 256-particle source tile in shared memory lets 256 target threads reuse the tile while retaining one thread per target and the original interaction order. This may reduce repeated source loads, though the synchronization cost per tile could offset gains, particularly at smaller sizes.
notes: This is an unmeasured candidate. The supplied baseline is correct on 11 cases with mean time 0.00185514 s; no candidate correctness or speedup is claimed. The controller should run the full correctness checks and compare the scored sizes.
transformations: Stage up to 256 source particles per block in dynamic shared memory, allocated as 256 * 28 bytes.
Keep one thread per target; traverse source tiles in increasing order and skip self-interaction by index.
Synchronize all threads before reading each staged tile and before reusing shared storage; keep inactive tail threads participating in barriers.
Retain the original integration and complete Particle output state.
